description: Doctor asks git whether .claude/worktrees is ignored, spec draft says to commit before accepting, a library word in the objective outranks an API word, and a closed pipe ends hexa quietly; nothing else changes.

specs.description: An ignore entry in .git/info/exclude counts
specs.given: A git repository with a .claude/worktrees directory, no mention of it in the root .gitignore, and the line `.claude/worktrees` in .git/info/exclude
specs.when: `hexa doctor` is run in the repository
specs.then: Doctor does not warn that .claude/worktrees is not ignored

specs.description: An ignore entry in the global excludes file counts
specs.given: A git repository with a .claude/worktrees directory, no mention of it in .gitignore or .git/info/exclude, and core.excludesFile pointing at a file that lists `.claude/worktrees`
specs.then: Doctor does not warn that .claude/worktrees is not ignored

specs.description: A path ignored by the root .gitignore is still accepted
specs.given: A git repository whose root .gitignore lists `.claude/worktrees`
specs.then: Doctor does not warn that .claude/worktrees is not ignored

specs.description: A path git does not ignore is still reported
specs.given: A git repository with a .claude/worktrees directory that no .gitignore, .git/info/exclude or global excludes file ignores, so `git check-ignore .claude/worktrees` exits non-zero
specs.then: Doctor warns that .claude/worktrees is not ignored

specs.description: A negation that un-ignores the path is respected
specs.given: A git repository whose .git/info/exclude lists `.claude/worktrees` but whose root .gitignore contains `!.claude/worktrees`, so `git check-ignore .claude/worktrees` reports it is not ignored
specs.then: Doctor warns that .claude/worktrees is not ignored

specs.description: Outside a git repository only .gitignore is read
specs.given: A directory that is not a git repository, with a .claude/worktrees directory and a .gitignore that does not list it
specs.then: Doctor warns that .claude/worktrees is not ignored, as it did before this ADR, and does not fail because git has no repository

specs.description: Outside a git repository a .gitignore entry is honoured
specs.given: A directory that is not a git repository, whose .gitignore lists `.claude/worktrees`
specs.then: Doctor does not warn that .claude/worktrees is not ignored

specs.description: Doctor's verdict agrees with git
specs.given: Any git repository and any combination of .gitignore, .git/info/exclude and global excludes contents
specs.then: Doctor warns that .claude/worktrees is not ignored if and only if `git check-ignore .claude/worktrees` reports it is not ignored

specs.description: The draft's closing line names the file, says to commit, then says to accept
specs.given: A repository with an ADR that has no spec yet
specs.then: Its closing output names the written spec file's path, tells the user to commit that file, and after that names `hexa spec accept <ADR>`

specs.description: Following the instruction succeeds
specs.given: A spec just written by `hexa spec draft <ADR>`
specs.when: The user commits the named spec file as instructed and then runs `hexa spec accept <ADR>`
specs.then: `hexa spec accept` does not refuse on the grounds that the spec is untracked or modified

specs.description: The draft no longer tells the user to accept an uncommitted spec directly
specs.given: A repository with an ADR that has no spec yet
specs.then: Its closing output does not tell the user to run `hexa spec accept <ADR>` without first committing the spec

specs.description: Accept still refuses an uncommitted first acceptance
specs.given: A spec written by `hexa spec draft <ADR>` that has not been committed
specs.then: It refuses, as ADR-2611161600 §1 requires, and names `git add` and `git commit`

specs.description: An SDK for an API is a library
specs.given: A project with no detected web framework and the objective "a Python SDK for the Example API"
specs.then: The output type is library, and no constraint such as "Return JSON responses with appropriate HTTP status codes" appears in session context

specs.description: Each library word outranks API words
specs.given: A project with no detected web framework whose objective names one of library, crate, package, SDK or framework together with one of api, server, rest, http or endpoint, and no CLI word
specs.then: The output type is library

specs.description: A detected web framework still wins
specs.given: A project in which a web framework is detected and whose objective reads "a client library for the HTTP API"
specs.then: The output type is a web API, as before, not a library

specs.description: The CLI check still comes first
specs.given: A project with no detected web framework whose objective names a command-line tool and also names an SDK and an API
specs.then: The output type is whatever the CLI check yields today, not library

specs.description: An API objective with no library word is still a web API
specs.given: A project with no detected web framework and the objective "a REST server exposing HTTP endpoints"
specs.then: The output type is a web API, as before

specs.description: Library words outrank API words for every objective
specs.given: Any objective containing at least one library word, with no web framework detected and the CLI check not matching
specs.then: The output type is library, whatever API words the objective also contains

specs.description: Piping analyze into head leaves no core
specs.given: A Unix system with core dumps enabled and a project whose `hexa analyze .` output is longer than ten lines
specs.then: head prints its lines, hexa prints no panic message on stderr, and no core file appears in the working directory

specs.description: Piping spec show into head leaves no core
specs.given: A Unix system with core dumps enabled and an ADR whose `hexa spec show <ADR>` output is longer than ten lines
specs.then: hexa prints no panic message and no core file appears in the working directory

specs.description: A closed pipe does not produce a panic
specs.given: A Unix system and a hexa command writing to a pipe whose reader has closed
specs.then: hexa does not report a panic, does not abort and does not leave a core file; it ends by the default SIGPIPE disposition

specs.description: A full read of the pipe is unaffected
specs.given: A hexa command whose reader consumes all output, for example `hexa analyze . | cat`
specs.then: All output is delivered and the exit status is the same as when run without a pipe

specs.description: Every hexa command ends quietly on a closed pipe
specs.given: Any hexa subcommand that writes to stdout on Unix, and a reader that closes the pipe after any number of bytes
specs.then: The process ends with no panic message and no core file

specs.description: Other doctor checks report as before
specs.given: A repository in which a doctor check other than the .claude/worktrees ignore check fails
specs.then: That check reports the same result as before this ADR

specs.description: Accept refuses a modified first acceptance as before
specs.given: A spec that was committed and then modified in the working tree, never accepted
specs.then: It refuses, as it did before this ADR

specs.description: Failing commands keep their exit status
specs.given: A hexa command that fails for a reason other than a closed pipe, such as `hexa spec show` for an ADR that does not exist
specs.when: It is run with stdout attached to a terminal or a fully read pipe
specs.then: It exits with the same non-zero status as before this ADR

specs.description: Objectives with no library word keep their output type
specs.given: Any objective that contains none of library, crate, package, SDK or framework
specs.then: The output type is the same as before this ADR

specs.description: No exit status except a closed pipe's changes
specs.given: Any hexa invocation whose output is not written to a closed pipe
specs.then: Its exit status is the same as before this ADR

amendments.reason: Fixture defects only, no assertion changed: the fingerprint fixtures wrote the workplan objective under 'objective', which the extractor never reads (it reads 'description'); S26 used 'spec show' of a missing ADR as its failing command, which exits 0 before and after this ADR ('spec verify' of one fails); S09/S10's repository had no test home, and ran a real model call: it now has a Cargo.toml and a fake claude on PATH replying with a complete spec, as other spec draft tests do. 13 fail without the fix, 19 pass with it
